A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. All 18 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original detection, removal, defense, and supplementary experiments on Inj-SQuAD and Inj-TriviaQA, including Tables 1–5 and Figures 3 and 6.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results, including the appendix detection results and positional-generalization analysis.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same detection models, segmentation and extraction procedures, training losses, and removal operations.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same datasets, tasks, attack purposes, and injection positions. Table 6 corrects swapped category labels without changing the examples, category counts, or demonstrated coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated attack, detector, and defense baselines remain identical in the corresponding comparisons. Table 9's corrected Escape-Separation caption matches the attack already specified in Appendix A.2 of v2; it does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: Dataset construction, sample counts, injection-position proportions, evaluation metrics, model configurations, and training and generation settings remain unchanged, including Appendix A.1 and A.4.

E4.justification: The injection-rate sensitivity, positional generalization, in-domain versus out-of-domain over-defense, and clean-document utility analyses are unchanged in Figures 3 and 6 and Tables 1 and 4.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and reported findings in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3 and 6 are unchanged. Table 6 retains all counts and examples; its category-label correction does not revise an experimental outcome.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, and operations in Equations 1–7 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about detection difficulties, trained models, over-defense, removal effectiveness, and combined filtering.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning document fluency, model strength, injection position, and generalization remain unchanged. The limitations retain the same qualifications about removal effectiveness and exclusion of direct prompt injection.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, baseline descriptions, and evaluation instructions. Code-access information is unchanged; the Table 9 correction adds no previously undisclosed procedure.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged, including the distinction from direct-injection detection and the claimed gap in instruction removal.

P1.justification: Editing is limited to category and attack-name corrections in the appendix and the updated arXiv version/date stamp. The main prose, terminology, and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 6 exchanges the Phishing and Advertisement labels so they match the existing examples. Table 9's caption changes from Escape-Deletion to Escape-Separation. Figures, table structures, and placement otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 fixes two misleading appendix labels: Table 6 now correctly categorizes the advertisement and phishing examples, and Table 9 agrees with its example and Appendix A.2. These corrections modestly improve accuracy and consistency while leaving the scientific evidence and its limitations unchanged.
